playbook:
When hide stage opens and I'm alive, pick a central cell (5) on the first round.

When I'm hit in the previous round, move off my previous hide to an adjacent cell (±1) rather than staying put.

When the standing order assigns a target, follow the standing order and target that boat unless told otherwise by a clear tactical reason (Harbor warning, target already jettisoned).

When choosing a fire cell, reuse my current hide cell as my shot guess (i.e., fire the cell I'm hiding in) to keep my behavior simple and to exploit any symmetry or reaction patterns.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, always file the claim that exactly matches that private result (truthful claim).

Never fire on Harbor unless I'm explicitly willing to take the -3 to Harbor and +3 to myself; treat Harbor as effectively off-limits by default.

When naming an escort (salvage), only name an actual live picket boat (Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma, Harbor if alive). Do not invent names; invalid escort claims are pointless and may be disallowed.

When I want escort points, coordinate to create a mutual escort claim with one other live boat (each names the other the same round). If no mutual agreement is possible, claim none.

If I have been repeatedly missing the same target with no new information, vary my shot cell by moving it one step (±1) from the last fired cell rather than jumping randomly.

If I suspect an opponent is patterning their hides (they hit me or I hit them), bias my subsequent hides toward cells consistent with that pattern to exploit predictability.

When composing public notes, keep them bland and consistent with my chosen station posture (e.g., "steady on station") to avoid signaling deceptive patterns unless I'm attempting a coordinated mutual escort or deception; in that case, make the minimal necessary note.

When uncertain whether a claimed escort will be reciprocated, do not commit to an escort claim that relies on an opponent naming a nonexistent boat.

When I get evidence that a particular opponent favors a specific cell (from hits/misses timing), preferentially fire that cell when they are my standing-order target.

If a line of play (e.g., claiming escorts with nonexistent boats) fails or is disallowed, stop immediately and revert to valid direct actions: truthful shot claims, valid escort names, and following standing-order targeting.

1.text:
When asked for hide, pick a cell different from my previous hide; prefer central cells early only if I have no pattern to exploit, otherwise vary to avoid predictability.

When given the standing order target, follow it unless firing on Harbor is ordered — never fire on Harbor unless I can tolerate the penalty and there is a decisive scoring reason.

When choosing a firing coordinate, use a small local search pattern around my last hide if I suspect another boat is shooting my cell; otherwise choose a fresh cell (do not repeat the same hide number every round).

When the office privately tells me my shot result, echo that result publicly exactly (claim must match private result).

When I score a hit on a boat, continue to prioritize firing at that boat on subsequent opportunities only if the standing order or tactical situation supports it; do not assume the same cell will produce repeated hits.

When posting a station note, keep it short and noncommittal (e.g., "steady on station" or "holding position") to avoid revealing hiding patterns.

When naming an escort, name another boat only if I have a reasonable expectation they will name me back; otherwise claim none (false or unilateral escort claims are low value).

When I detect symmetric mutual support potential (other boat likely to reciprocate escort), coordinate notes to increase chance of a mutual escort and collect the 5-point bonus.

When a round summary shows repeated misses from a particular opponent at my hide, change hide patterns away from cells they have targeted.

If forced into a high-risk/ high-reward decision about firing on Harbor for payroll reasons, calculate the net expected value first; by default avoid attacking Harbor.

Do not lock into a single hide number across rounds — repeating the same hide made me predictable and is a mistake.

2.text:
When asked to hide, pick a cell that is not an obvious repeat of my prior hides; alternate between center and an edge and occasionally pick a high/low extreme so my pattern is hard to guess. If I just got hit, change quadrant from my last hide.

When told the standing order target, fire at that named boat unless there is a compelling tactical reason not to (see exceptions). Do not fire at Harbor unless Harbor has already been forced off the board and the rules allow — firing at Harbor incurs a heavy guaranteed penalty and is not worth it.

When choosing a fire cell against a boat, do not repeat a cell that I fired earlier at the same target if that shot missed. Use past hit/miss history against that target (my own and observed public claims) to eliminate cells and bias toward untried cells in the same quadrant as any observed hits. If I have no information, pick a moderately central cell (not the same as previous moderate choices every round).

When I receive my private shot result, always file the required public claim that matches it exactly — truthful claiming is mandatory.

When composing my station note, keep it generic and nonrevealing (e.g., "steady on station") unless I can exploit a predictable opponent reaction: mimic other boats' notes to blend in or use neutral phrasing to avoid giving location hints.

When deciding an escort claim, only claim an escort if I am confident the other boat will reciprocate this round (based on prior mutual behavior). If I cannot reasonably expect reciprocation, claim none — random solo escort claims are wasted opportunities and produce no points.

When I notice another boat repeatedly targeting the same opponent and getting misses, assume they are using a narrow predictable set of cells; exploit that by varying my own firing to different cells to gain hits. Conversely, when an opponent scores a hit on a target, infer the hit cell's neighborhood and try adjacent cells on subsequent attacks against that target.

When my score is behind and there is an opportunity to get a hit by deviating from the standing order, consider breaking order only if the expected gain minus risk (including any Harbor penalty) is favorable. Otherwise follow the standing order to avoid chaotic mistakes.

When behavior in prior rounds shows my choices were too predictable (e.g., repeating the same fire cell or hiding spot), explicitly change pattern next decision rather than subtle variation — big enough change to be nonobvious.

When I lack information, prioritize survival of points over risky plays: avoid attacking Harbor, avoid making escort claims without reciprocation, and avoid repeating failed shots.
